scenes.line: The AI boom just stopped paying for itself. For twenty years, big tech's cash covered any investment with billions to spare. Not this year.
The test is one number. Cash from operations, minus capital spending, equals free cash flow.
The four biggest data-centre builders, latest quarter, one scale. Blue is cash in, orange is what they spent.
Three of the four came out below zero.
Alphabet: minus five point nine billion. Its first negative quarter since it listed in two thousand and four.
Amazon: minus eight point eight billion, plus thirteen and a half billion of new long-term debt.
Oracle: minus five point four billion, the fifth negative quarter in a row. Half its cash in was customer prepayments.
Microsoft is the exception: nineteen billion positive, but twenty-three percent less than a year ago.
Add Meta, and the five hyperscalers will spend about eight hundred and twenty billion this year, against seven hundred and fifty billion of cash from operations. The gap is debt and equity.
A self-funded build-out can slow down quietly. A leveraged one needs the AI revenue to show up, on a schedule. Worth watching which happens first.
